newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil private coffee sector, govt to meet April 11.
newsitem.headline: Brazil private coffee sector, govt to meet April 11.

text.p: Brazil representatives from the private coffee sector will now meet government officials on April 11 in Sao Paulo after a meeting planned this afternoon was postponed, private sector officials said.
"I think it just didn't suit someone to hold the meeting today," one official said.

The meeting will unite all the members of Brazil's new coffee council, the CDPC, and the main topic of discussions will be the agenda of the next full session of the council, scheduled for May 5 in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais state.

Officials are unlikely however to discuss Brazil's position on market stabilisation plans from July 1997 amongst members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation (FEBEC).
The ACPC secretariat has asked members to send any suggestions to London by April 15.

Rather Brazil's stance is likely to be discussed by top commodity official Mauricio Assis and exporters at the next regular session to discuss the progress of exports, said Aranha, adding, ""We, FEBEC, will put forward a position on the ACPC."
No date had been set however for a meeting between Assis and FEBEC representatives, he added.
